name: Employee Benefit Plan Financial Statements (Area II)
topic: Employee Benefit Plan Financial Statements (Area II)

questions.subtopic: Required Financial Statements — Defined Benefit Plan
questions.stem: Rowan Industries Retirement Plan is a defined benefit pension plan that issues its own annual financial statements as a separate reporting entity under ASC 960. Which of the following describes the complete set of information that the plan is required to present?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A statement of net assets available for benefits, a statement of changes in net assets available for benefits, information about the actuarial present value of accumulated plan benefits, and information about the year-to-year changes in that actuarial present value

choices.label: B
choices.text: A balance sheet, a statement of operations, a statement of changes in participants' equity, and a statement of cash flows

choices.label: C
choices.text: A statement of net assets available for benefits and a statement of changes in net assets available for benefits only, because the benefit obligation is presented solely by the sponsoring employer

choices.label: D
choices.text: A statement of net assets available for benefits, a statement of cash flows, and a reconciliation of the plan's funded status to the net pension liability recognized by the sponsoring employer

questions.explanation: ASC 960-205-45 requires a defined benefit plan's annual financial statements to present four things: (1) a statement of net assets available for benefits at the end of the plan year, (2) a statement of changes in net assets available for benefits for the year, (3) information regarding the actuarial present value of accumulated plan benefits, and (4) information regarding the effects of significant factors that changed that actuarial present value during the year. The last two items may be presented as separate statements, combined with the net asset statements, or presented in the notes. A commercial-style balance sheet, statement of operations and statement of changes in participants' equity are not the prescribed plan statements; a plan reports net assets available for benefits, not equity. Limiting the presentation to the two net asset statements and omitting the benefit obligation information is the defined contribution model under ASC 962, not the defined benefit model. A statement of cash flows is encouraged only when it would provide relevant information and is not required, and the reconciliation of funded status to a recognized net pension liability is an employer-level ASC 715 disclosure that has no place in the plan's own statements.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 960-205-45 は、確定給付年金制度が自ら作成する財務諸表として次の4つの情報の表示を求めている。(1) 期末時点の給付に充当可能な純資産計算書、(2) 当期の給付に充当可能な純資産の変動計算書、(3) 累積給付債務の年金数理現在価値に関する情報、(4) 当該年金数理現在価値を当期に変動させた重要な要因の影響に関する情報。後の2つは独立した計算書、純資産計算書との結合表示、注記のいずれでも表示できる。企業型の貸借対照表・損益計算書・持分変動計算書は制度の所定様式ではない（制度は「持分」ではなく「給付に充当可能な純資産」を報告する）。純資産に関する2つの計算書だけに限定して給付債務情報を省略するのは ASC 962 の確定拠出制度のモデルであり、確定給付制度には当てはまらない。キャッシュ・フロー計算書は有用な情報を提供する場合に推奨されるにとどまり必須ではない。積立状況と認識済み年金負債の調整表は ASC 715 に基づく事業主側の開示であり、制度自身の財務諸表には含まれない。

questions.subtopic: Defined Contribution Plan vs Defined Benefit Plan Reporting
questions.stem: Halstead Savings Plan is a defined contribution 401(k) plan that prepares financial statements under ASC 962. How do the plan's financial statements differ from those of a defined benefit pension plan reporting under ASC 960?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The defined contribution plan presents the actuarial present value of accumulated plan benefits, while the defined benefit plan presents only net assets available for benefits

choices.label: B
choices.text: The defined contribution plan presents no actuarial present value of accumulated plan benefits, because the benefit is defined by the balances in individual participant accounts; it presents net assets available for benefits and the changes in those net assets

choices.label: C
choices.text: The defined contribution plan carries its investments at amortized cost, while the defined benefit plan carries its investments at fair value

choices.label: D
choices.text: The defined contribution plan is required to present a statement of cash flows, while the defined benefit plan is exempt from that requirement

questions.explanation: In a defined contribution plan the benefit a participant will receive is whatever accumulates in that participant's individual account, so there is no promised benefit formula to value actuarially. ASC 962-205-45 therefore requires only a statement of net assets available for benefits and a statement of changes in net assets available for benefits; no actuarial present value of accumulated plan benefits is presented. It is the defined benefit plan under ASC 960 that must present that actuarial information, so reversing the two plan types is incorrect. Both types of plans measure investments at fair value, not amortized cost, subject to the narrow contract-value exception for fully benefit-responsive investment contracts. Neither plan type is required to present a statement of cash flows; it is encouraged for both when it would provide relevant information, so the requirement cannot be a point of difference between them.
questions.explanationJa: 確定拠出制度では、参加者が受け取る給付は各自の個人勘定に積み上がった残高そのものであるため、年金数理評価の対象となる給付算定式が存在しない。したがって ASC 962-205-45 は、給付に充当可能な純資産計算書と同変動計算書のみを求め、累積給付債務の年金数理現在価値は表示しない。当該年金数理情報を表示しなければならないのは ASC 960 の確定給付制度の側であり、両者を逆に述べた記述は誤り。投資はいずれの制度でも償却原価ではなく公正価値で測定する（完全給付対応型投資契約を契約価額で測定する限定的な例外を除く）。キャッシュ・フロー計算書はいずれの制度でも必須ではなく、有用な場合に推奨されるにとどまるため、両者の相違点にはならない。

questions.subtopic: Actuarial Present Value of Accumulated Plan Benefits
questions.stem: Under ASC 960, the accumulated plan benefits that a defined benefit pension plan presents in its own financial statements are measured on which of the following bases?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Benefits attributable to service rendered through the benefit information date, measured using employees' projected compensation at expected retirement, presented as a single undivided amount

choices.label: B
choices.text: Benefits attributable to service rendered through the benefit information date, measured using employees' compensation history through that date, and segregated among vested benefits of participants currently receiving payments, other vested benefits, and nonvested benefits

choices.label: C
choices.text: Benefits expected to be paid to all current participants over their remaining lives, discounted at the plan's expected long-term rate of return on assets and presented net of the fair value of plan assets

choices.label: D
choices.text: The projected benefit obligation the sponsoring employer measures under ASC 715, carried forward unchanged so that the plan and the employer report the same obligation amount

questions.explanation: Accumulated plan benefits under ASC 960 are those future benefit payments attributable to employees' service rendered up to the benefit information date, and for pay-related plans they are measured using employees' compensation history through that date rather than projected future salary levels. The actuarial present value must be segregated into three categories: vested benefits of participants currently receiving payments, other vested benefits, and nonvested benefits. Using projected compensation at retirement describes the employer's projected benefit obligation under ASC 715, and a single undivided amount would violate the required three-way split. Discounting at the expected long-term rate of return and netting against plan assets is wrong on two counts: the assumed discount rate must reflect the rates at which the obligation could be effectively settled, and the plan presents net assets available for benefits separately from the benefit obligation rather than as one net amount. Carrying forward the employer's projected benefit obligation is also incorrect, because that measure includes projected salary increases and is deliberately not the plan-level measure.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 960 における累積給付債務（accumulated plan benefits）とは、給付情報日までに従業員が提供した勤務に帰属する将来の給付支払であり、給与比例型の制度では将来の昇給予測ではなく当該日までの給与実績にもとづいて測定する。その年金数理現在価値は、(1) 現に給付を受給中の参加者の受給権付給付、(2) その他の受給権付給付、(3) 受給権未付与の給付、の3区分に分けて表示しなければならない。退職時の予測給与を用いる測定は事業主側の ASC 715 に基づく予測給付債務（PBO）の説明であり、単一の未分割金額とするのも required な3区分表示に反する。期待長期運用収益率で割り引いて制度資産と相殺する方法は二重に誤りで、割引率は債務を実質的に決済しうる利率を反映しなければならず、また制度は給付に充当可能な純資産と給付債務を相殺せず別個に表示する。事業主の PBO をそのまま引き継ぐのも、PBO が将来の昇給を織り込む測定値であり制度レベルの測定値として意図的に用いられないため誤り。

questions.subtopic: Statement of Changes in Net Assets Available for Benefits
questions.stem:
Marbury Employees' Pension Plan reports the following for the year ended December 31, Year 6:

Net assets available for benefits, January 1 | $8,400,000
Employer contributions | $1,250,000
Participant contributions | $430,000
Net appreciation in fair value of investments | $620,000
Interest and dividend income | $315,000
Benefits paid to participants | $940,000
Administrative expenses | $85,000

What amount should the plan report as net assets available for benefits at December 31, Year 6?
questions.explanation: The statement of changes in net assets available for benefits accumulates all additions and deducts all deductions. Additions are the employer contributions of $1,250,000, the participant contributions of $430,000, the net appreciation in the fair value of investments of $620,000 and the interest and dividend income of $315,000, a total of $2,615,000. Deductions are the benefits paid of $940,000 and the administrative expenses of $85,000, a total of $1,025,000. The net increase of $1,590,000 added to the beginning balance of $8,400,000 gives ending net assets available for benefits of $9,990,000. The $9,560,000 result omits the $430,000 of participant contributions, which are an addition to plan net assets even though the employer did not fund them. The $9,370,000 result excludes the $620,000 net appreciation on the theory that unrealized gains are not recognized; plan investments are carried at fair value and both realized and unrealized changes are reported as net appreciation. The $10,075,000 result fails to deduct the $85,000 of administrative expenses paid by the plan.
questions.explanationJa: 給付に充当可能な純資産の変動計算書は、すべての増加項目を集計し、すべての減少項目を控除する。増加項目は事業主拠出 $1,250,000、参加者拠出 $430,000、投資の公正価値の純増価額 $620,000、受取利息・配当 $315,000 の合計 $2,615,000。減少項目は給付支払 $940,000 と管理費用 $85,000 の合計 $1,025,000。差引の純増加 $1,590,000 を期首残高 $8,400,000 に加算し、期末の給付に充当可能な純資産は $9,990,000 となる。$9,560,000 は参加者拠出 $430,000 を除外したもので、事業主が拠出したものでなくとも制度の純資産の増加項目である。$9,370,000 は未実現利益を認識しないとして純増価額 $620,000 を除外したものだが、制度の投資は公正価値で計上され、実現・未実現いずれの変動も net appreciation として報告する。$10,075,000 は制度が負担した管理費用 $85,000 を控除し忘れた金額。

questions.subtopic: Statement of Changes — Solve for Benefits Paid
questions.stem:
Delphine Retirement Plan's statement of changes in net assets available for benefits for the year ended December 31, Year 4 includes the following:

Net assets available for benefits, January 1 | $5,200,000
Total contributions (employer and participant) | $900,000
Net investment income, including net appreciation | $460,000
Administrative expenses | $60,000
Net assets available for benefits, December 31 | $5,700,000

Benefits paid to participants were the only other item reported. What amount of benefits did the plan pay during Year 4?
questions.explanation: Beginning net assets of $5,200,000 plus contributions of $900,000 plus net investment income of $460,000 equals $6,560,000 before deductions. Deducting the $60,000 of administrative expenses leaves $6,500,000, so benefits paid must be $6,500,000 less the ending balance of $5,700,000, or $800,000. The $860,000 answer ignores the administrative expenses, treating the entire $6,560,000 as available before benefits. The $920,000 answer adds the $60,000 of administrative expenses as though they were an addition rather than a deduction. The $340,000 answer omits the $460,000 of net investment income from the additions, which understates the amount available and therefore understates the benefits that could have been paid.
questions.explanationJa: 期首純資産 $5,200,000 に拠出 $900,000 と純投資収益 $460,000 を加えると、控除前で $6,560,000 となる。管理費用 $60,000 を控除すると $6,500,000 となり、給付支払額は $6,500,000 から期末残高 $5,700,000 を差し引いた $800,000 である。$860,000 は管理費用を無視し、$6,560,000 全額が給付支払前の残高であるとしたもの。$920,000 は管理費用 $60,000 を減少項目ではなく増加項目として加算した誤り。$340,000 は純投資収益 $460,000 を増加項目から除外したもので、利用可能額を過小にするため給付支払額も過小になる。

questions.subtopic: Net Appreciation in Fair Value of Investments
questions.stem:
Ashgrove Pension Plan reports its investments at fair value. During the year ended December 31, Year 7:

Investments at fair value, January 1 | $3,000,000
Investments at fair value, December 31 | $3,450,000
Purchases of investments during the year | $500,000
Proceeds from sales of investments during the year | $380,000

The purchases were funded by employer contributions, the sales proceeds were held in cash at year end, and all dividend and interest income was received in cash and was not reinvested. What amount of net appreciation in the fair value of investments should the plan report in its statement of changes in net assets available for benefits?
questions.explanation: Net appreciation is the change in the fair value of investments that is not explained by purchases and sales. Beginning investments of $3,000,000 plus purchases of $500,000 less the $380,000 of investments disposed of at their sales proceeds equals $3,120,000 of investments that would be on hand absent any change in value. Because the ending fair value is $3,450,000, the net appreciation, realized and unrealized combined, is $330,000. The $450,000 answer is simply the change in the investment balance and ignores that $500,000 of new money was invested and $380,000 was withdrawn from the portfolio. The $570,000 answer reverses the signs by adding purchases and subtracting sales. The $830,000 answer adds the sales proceeds to the change in balance, double counting investments that had already been removed from the portfolio.
questions.explanationJa: 純増価額（net appreciation）とは、投資の公正価値の変動のうち購入と売却では説明できない部分をいう。期首投資 $3,000,000 に購入 $500,000 を加え、売却代金 $380,000 相当の処分分を差し引くと $3,120,000 となり、これが価値変動がなかった場合の残高である。期末公正価値が $3,450,000 であるから、実現・未実現を合わせた純増価額は $330,000 となる。$450,000 は単なる投資残高の増減であり、新たに $500,000 が投資され $380,000 が引き出された事実を無視している。$570,000 は符号を逆にして購入を加算し売却を減算した誤り。$830,000 は残高の増減に売却代金を加算したもので、すでにポートフォリオから除かれた投資を二重計上している。

questions.subtopic: Statement of Net Assets Available for Benefits
questions.stem:
Thornbury Employees' Pension Plan reports the following at December 31, Year 5:

Investments, at fair value (cost $6,100,000) | $6,800,000
Cash | $150,000
Employer contribution receivable | $220,000
Participant contributions receivable | $45,000
Accrued interest and dividends receivable | $35,000
Accounts payable for administrative expenses | $40,000
Benefits payable to participants who elected to withdraw but had not been paid at year end | $180,000

What amount should the plan report as net assets available for benefits at December 31, Year 5?
questions.explanation: Plan assets are measured at fair value, so the investments enter at $6,800,000 rather than their $6,100,000 cost. Adding cash of $150,000, the employer contribution receivable of $220,000, the participant contributions receivable of $45,000 and accrued interest and dividends receivable of $35,000 gives total assets of $7,250,000. The only liability deducted is the $40,000 of accounts payable for administrative expenses, producing net assets available for benefits of $7,210,000. Amounts payable to participants who have elected to withdraw but have not yet been paid are not recognized as a liability of the plan under GAAP; they remain in net assets available for benefits and are instead disclosed in the notes, which is why the $7,030,000 figure that deducts the $180,000 is wrong. The $6,510,000 figure improperly carries the investments at their $6,100,000 cost. The $6,910,000 figure omits the $300,000 of contributions and income receivable, which are assets of the plan because they are due to the plan at the reporting date.
questions.explanationJa: 制度の資産は公正価値で測定するため、投資は取得原価 $6,100,000 ではなく $6,800,000 で計上する。これに現金 $150,000、事業主拠出未収金 $220,000、参加者拠出未収金 $45,000、未収利息・配当 $35,000 を加えると資産合計は $7,250,000 となる。控除する負債は管理費用の未払金 $40,000 のみであり、給付に充当可能な純資産は $7,210,000 となる。脱退を選択したが年度末時点で未払の参加者への給付支払債務は、US GAAP では制度の負債として認識せず、給付に充当可能な純資産に含めたまま注記で開示する。したがって $180,000 を控除した $7,030,000 は誤り。$6,510,000 は投資を取得原価 $6,100,000 のままにした誤り。$6,910,000 は報告日時点で制度に対して支払われるべき資産である拠出未収金・未収収益 合計 $300,000 を除外している。

questions.subtopic: Statement of Net Assets — Defined Contribution Plan Measurement
questions.stem:
Caldwell Savings Plan, a defined contribution 401(k) plan, reports the following at December 31, Year 5:

Mutual funds, at fair value (cost $8,600,000) | $9,400,000
Fully benefit-responsive guaranteed investment contract — contract value | $1,200,000
Fully benefit-responsive guaranteed investment contract — fair value | $1,150,000
Notes receivable from participants (participant loans) — unpaid principal | $260,000
Notes receivable from participants (participant loans) — fair value | $250,000
Employer contribution receivable | $140,000
Accrued administrative expenses payable | $30,000

What amount should the plan report as net assets available for benefits at December 31, Year 5?
questions.explanation: The mutual funds are measured at their fair value of $9,400,000, not their $8,600,000 cost. A fully benefit-responsive investment contract is measured at contract value, the amount participants would receive on a benefit-responsive transaction, so the guaranteed investment contract enters at $1,200,000 rather than its $1,150,000 fair value. Participant loans are classified as notes receivable from participants rather than as investments and are measured at unpaid principal plus accrued interest, so they enter at $260,000 rather than $250,000. Adding the $140,000 employer contribution receivable and deducting the $30,000 of accrued administrative expenses gives net assets available for benefits of $10,970,000. The $10,910,000 result incorrectly measures both the investment contract and the participant loans at fair value. The $10,170,000 result carries the mutual funds at cost. The $10,710,000 result omits the participant loans entirely, but the loans are an asset of the plan and are reported separately from investments.
questions.explanationJa: 投資信託は取得原価 $8,600,000 ではなく公正価値 $9,400,000 で測定する。完全給付対応型投資契約（fully benefit-responsive investment contract）は、給付事由の発生時に参加者が受け取る金額である契約価額で測定するため、公正価値 $1,150,000 ではなく $1,200,000 で計上する。参加者向け貸付金は投資ではなく「参加者からの未収金（notes receivable from participants）」に分類し、未払元本に未収利息を加えた額で測定するため、$250,000 ではなく $260,000 で計上する。これに事業主拠出未収金 $140,000 を加え、未払管理費用 $30,000 を控除すると、給付に充当可能な純資産は $10,970,000 となる。$10,910,000 は投資契約と参加者貸付金の双方を誤って公正価値で測定したもの。$10,170,000 は投資信託を取得原価のままにしたもの。$10,710,000 は参加者貸付金を丸ごと除外しているが、同貸付金は制度の資産であり投資とは区分して表示する。

questions.subtopic: Note Disclosures — Plan Description and Investment Concentration
questions.stem: Which of the following must be disclosed in the notes to the financial statements of an employee benefit plan?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A description of the plan agreement, including vesting and benefit provisions and any plan amendments adopted during the year, and the identification of any single investment that represents 5% or more of net assets available for benefits

choices.label: B
choices.text: The sponsoring employer's net periodic pension cost for the year and the components used to compute it, so that readers can reconcile the plan's results to the sponsor's income statement

choices.label: C
choices.text: The account balance of each individual participant at the reporting date, listed by participant name, together with each participant's vested percentage

choices.label: D
choices.text: A reconciliation of the plan's net assets available for benefits to the sponsoring employer's consolidated stockholders' equity

questions.explanation: Plan financial statements must include a general description of the plan agreement, covering matters such as the participant groups covered, vesting and benefit provisions, the plan's funding policy, the priority of claims on termination, and any plan amendments adopted during the year. Plans must also disclose significant concentrations of investment risk by identifying any individual investment, other than issues of the U.S. government, that represents 5% or more of net assets available for benefits. Net periodic pension cost is an employer measure computed under ASC 715 and is not reported by the plan, whose expense captions are benefits paid and administrative expenses. A participant-by-participant listing of account balances is not a financial statement disclosure and would defeat the aggregate nature of plan reporting. There is no requirement to reconcile plan net assets to the sponsor's stockholders' equity; the plan's assets are held in trust for participants and are not the sponsor's equity.
questions.explanationJa: 制度の財務諸表の注記には、対象となる参加者グループ、受給権付与および給付の規定、資金拠出方針、制度終了時の請求権の優先順位、当期に採択された制度変更など、制度の内容の概要を記載しなければならない。また、米国政府発行のものを除き、給付に充当可能な純資産の5%以上を占める個別の投資を特定することで、投資リスクの重要な集中を開示する必要がある。純期間年金費用（net periodic pension cost）は ASC 715 に基づく事業主側の測定値であり制度は報告しない。制度側の費用項目は給付支払と管理費用である。参加者ごとの勘定残高の一覧は財務諸表の開示事項ではなく、集計ベースで報告するという制度会計の性格にも反する。制度の純資産を事業主の株主資本と調整する要求も存在しない。制度の資産は参加者のために信託されており、事業主の資本ではないからである。

questions.subtopic: Note Disclosures — Fair Value Hierarchy and Parties in Interest
questions.stem: Rutherford Employees' Plan measures its investments at fair value and invests part of its portfolio in a collective trust fund measured using net asset value per share as a practical expedient. Which statement about the plan's fair value and related party note disclosures is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Investments measured using net asset value per share as a practical expedient must still be assigned to Level 1, Level 2 or Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy so that the hierarchy table totals agree to total investments

choices.label: B
choices.text: The plan discloses the level within the fair value hierarchy for investments measured at fair value on a recurring basis, and separately discloses transactions with parties in interest such as the plan sponsor and the trustee

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because plan assets are held in trust for the exclusive benefit of participants, the plan is exempt from the fair value hierarchy disclosures that ASC 820 requires of other reporting entities

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transactions with parties in interest must be disclosed only when the amount involved exceeds 5% of the plan's net assets available for benefits

questions.explanation: A plan is a reporting entity subject to the ASC 820 fair value framework, so it discloses the level of the fair value hierarchy in which each class of recurring fair value measurement falls, along with the valuation techniques and inputs used for Level 2 and Level 3. It also discloses transactions with parties in interest, a category that includes the plan sponsor, the trustee, the investment manager and other service providers, because those transactions are related party transactions from the plan's perspective. Investments measured at net asset value per share as a practical expedient are excluded from the hierarchy and are presented separately to reconcile to total investments, so requiring them to be forced into a level is incorrect. Holding assets in trust for participants does not create an exemption from ASC 820; the trust arrangement affects who benefits from the assets, not how they are measured and disclosed. The 5% threshold applies to identifying a concentration in a single investment, not to party-in-interest transactions, which are disclosed regardless of size when significant to an understanding of the plan.
questions.explanationJa: 制度は ASC 820 の公正価値の枠組みが適用される報告主体であり、経常的に公正価値で測定する投資の各区分について公正価値ヒエラルキーのどのレベルに属するかを開示し、レベル2・レベル3については評価技法とインプットも開示する。あわせて、制度の視点からは関係当事者取引にあたる parties in interest（制度のスポンサー、受託者、運用管理者その他の役務提供者を含む）との取引も開示する。実務上の簡便法として1口当たり純資産価額（NAV）で測定する投資はヒエラルキーから除外し、投資合計との調整のため区分表示するため、無理にいずれかのレベルへ割り当てるという記述は誤り。資産が参加者のために信託されていることは ASC 820 の免除事由とはならず、信託という形態は誰が資産の便益を受けるかに関わる事項であって測定・開示の方法を変えるものではない。5%という閾値は個別投資の集中の特定に用いる基準であって parties in interest との取引には適用されず、当該取引は制度の理解に重要である限り金額の多寡を問わず開示する。
